audit.whatIsWrong: All seven chart rows disagree with the packet. Content and full read Graves/Skill/Yasuo/Yasuo/Graves/Yasuo/Yasuo; the packet reads Yasuo/Yasuo/Graves/Skill/Yasuo/Graves/Yasuo. The prose matches the packet on every row — whys[0] and whys[1] describe Yasuo poking freely, whys[2] calls 3 'this short window' for you, whys[3] says 'genuinely even', whys[4] is his level-6 kill chain, whys[5] says your first item beats his.
audit.why: The chart claimed Graves wins level 1 against a champion who pokes at 475 with a 4-second Q and dashes off the wave on a sub-1-second E, and gave Yasuo the first-item window that the text explicitly calls yours. Both errors point the player into fights at the wrong times in a 43.66% lane.
audit.corrected: All seven rows set to the packet chart, ratings 3/3/6/5/3/6/2.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level-6 spike never states that Last Breath is 70/50/30s. Wind Wall's 25/23/21/19/17s and 4-second duration are also missing, despite the entire win condition being 'commit on Wind Wall's cooldown'.
audit.why: 'Wait for Wind Wall' is unusable without the number. 25 seconds at rank 1 is a real window; by rank 5 it is 17 and the plan needs adjusting. Last Breath dropping to 30s late is why the late game is unplayable.
audit.corrected: Wind Wall's 4s duration and 25s rank-1 cooldown and Last Breath's 70s added to early, mid and whys[2].

audit.whatIsWrong: The Wind Wall interaction itself is handled correctly and thoroughly — shells, Q powder trail and R are all flagged projectile in the Graves kit and the page says so. The errors are Graves-side boilerplate: 'second E charge' and 'two E charges' four times (Quickdraw is one dash on 16/15/14/13/12s, refreshed by landing autos); 'blind his crit-autos' with Smoke Screen four times (W reduces sight range and slows on impact, it does not blind); 'your Q cone' (Q detonates, the cone is R); and dosFull[2] 'Hold R as the disengage knockback' (Collateral Damage has no displacement). wants.you[0] also tells you to go in 'before the wall expires', which is exactly backwards — the wall is what stops your damage.
audit.why: Against the one champion whose W deletes your entire projectile kit, telling the player to commit while the wall is still up is the single worst instruction on the page.
audit.corrected: Charges removed, W described as sight denial plus slow, Q as a detonation, R as a nuke, and the wants.you[0] timing inverted to after the 4 seconds run out.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[2].d calls a wasted Wind Wall a 'fifteen-second invitation'.
audit.why: Wind Wall is 25s at rank 1. Understating the window makes the player rush the commit and arrive with shells unloaded.

The page already carries the non-obvious part — that Graves' basic attacks are projectiles and therefore wallable, not just his abilities. That is the mechanic most Graves players get wrong here and it is stated plainly.

edits.before: Four shells of buckshot win any level-1 face-off — trade autos point-blank where every pellet lands.
edits.after: One dash, short shell range and no burst yet — he pokes with Steel Tempest and just walks away on E.

edits.before: E online — dash-reload weaving starts: auto, E for the grit armor and reset, auto again. Most champs lose this flat.
edits.after: He pokes with Steel Tempest and dashes off the minion wave on a near-zero cooldown E — you cannot pin him yet.

edits.before: Collateral Damage adds an execute and a disengage knockback in one — hold it for either, never for chip.
edits.after: Last Breath needs only a knockup and his third-Q tornado supplies it — never be the airborne one at 6.

edits.before: You out-skirmish but the crit scalers pass you — convert to picks with smoke-screen blinds and R snipes.
edits.after: Crit shred plus a Wind Wall that eats every shell you own — take picks elsewhere and end the game.

edits.before: Hold R as the disengage knockback
edits.after: Hold R to finish, never to chip

edits.before: Yasuo burns Wind Wall on nothing — take the fifteen-second invitation.
edits.after: Yasuo burns Wind Wall on nothing — that is 25 seconds of invitation at rank 1.

edits.before: Play assassin-marksman: smoke their engage, E through fights for armor, and save R as either the execute or the peel knockback. Crit carries out-DPS you — picks don't care.
edits.after: Play assassin-marksman: smoke their engage, E through fights for armor, and never fire the 100-second R into a live Wind Wall. Crit carries out-DPS you — picks don't care.

edits.before: Your W smoke blinds tower dives and breaks gank pathing — drop it on arrival and turn their 2v1 into a coin flip you win.
edits.after: Your W smoke nearsights tower dives and breaks gank pathing — drop it on arrival and turn their 2v1 into a coin flip you win.

edits.before: Fully online at 3: your second E charge to close, the point-blank shell spread, and W to blind his crit-autos win this short window if Windwall is down.
edits.after: Fully online at 3: Quickdraw to close, the point-blank shell spread and a Smoke Screen that blanks his sight win this window if Wind Wall's 25s is down.

edits.before: Your True Grit resists and two E charges hold the trade, but his crit shred out-stats that armor -- genuinely even and read-dependent.
edits.after: True Grit resists and a Quickdraw your autos refresh hold the trade, but his crit shred out-stats that armor -- even and read-dependent.

edits.before: Your one window: at 3 you have your second E charge to close, the point-blank 4-shell spread, and W to blind his crit-autos -- force a short trade while his Q tornado stack is still building.
edits.after: Your one window: at 3 you have Quickdraw to close, the point-blank 4-shell spread, and a Smoke Screen that blanks his sight -- force a short trade while his Q tornado stack is still building.

edits.before: His R Last Breath is the threat: he only needs you airborne, and a third-Q tornado supplies the knockup to chain it -- and his Windwall has likely already eaten your Q cone, your shells, or your R in the same fight.
edits.after: His R Last Breath is the threat, and only 70s at rank 1: he needs you airborne, and a third-Q tornado supplies the knockup -- while Wind Wall has likely already eaten your Q, your shells or your R in the same fight.

edits.before: Yasuo's Windwall (W) is the whole problem: your shell autoattacks, your Q powder trail, and your R are all projectiles, so a well-timed wall eats your entire burst and leaves you reloading for nothing. At 1-2 he pokes with Q and dashes through the minion wave on E (Sweeping Blade) -- which has only a short per-target cooldown -- so you can't pin him down. Your one real opening is level 3, when your second E charge and the point-blank 4-shell spread come online: E-in, blind his crit-autos with your W smoke, and burst him before his third-Q tornado is up.
edits.after: Yasuo's Windwall (W) is the whole problem: your shell autoattacks, your Q powder trail, and your R are all projectiles, so a well-timed wall eats your entire burst for its full 4 seconds and leaves you reloading for nothing. At 1-2 he pokes with Q and dashes through the minion wave on E (Sweeping Blade) -- which has only a short per-target cooldown -- so you can't pin him down. Your one real opening is level 3, when Quickdraw and the point-blank 4-shell spread come online: E-in, drop smoke so he loses sight of you, and burst him before his third-Q tornado is up.

edits.before: At 4-5 your True Grit passive stacks armor and MR while you stay in combat, and your two E charges let you survive a trade, but he's a gap-closer who out-stats that resistance with crit and ignores your kiting by dashing off the minion wave on E. Level 6 is his window, not yours: a third-Q tornado knocks you up and lets Last Breath chain his full crit combo, and if your Windwall read is wrong your R just gets walled. Your one comeback beat is first item -- Eclipse or Youmuu's gives you peak duel tempo, so force the all-in the moment his Windwall is on cooldown.
edits.after: At 4-5 your True Grit passive stacks armor and MR while you stay in combat, and a Quickdraw your autos keep refreshing lets you survive a trade, but he's a gap-closer who out-stats that resistance with crit and ignores your kiting by dashing off the minion wave on E. Level 6 is his window, not yours: a third-Q tornado knocks you up and Last Breath -- 70s at rank 1 -- chains his full crit combo, and a wrong Wind Wall read just walls your R. Your one comeback beat is first item: Eclipse or Youmuu's is peak duel tempo, so all-in the moment Wind Wall's 25 seconds start.

edits.before: Bait his Windwall (W) onto a single Q cone or your R, then E-in for the point-blank shell spread before the wall expires
edits.after: Bait his Windwall (W) with a single Q or an auto, then E-in for the point-blank shell spread once its 4 seconds run out

edits.before: Win the level 3 window: blind his crit-autos with your W smoke while you out-DPS him in melee range
edits.after: Win the level 3 window: cut his sight with W smoke and slow him while you out-damage him in melee
